entries.title: Biskup-Chayes (2003): mean-field bounds for discontinuous transitions
entries.statement: Biskup and Chayes study reflection-positive nearest-neighbor spin systems and derive a mean-field free-energy excess bound. For the nearest-neighbor integer-q Potts model, their Theorem 2.1 establishes a magnetization and energy jump at a coupling J_t for each fixed q>=3 when d is sufficiently large. The paper explicitly does not prove zero magnetization at every J<J_t.
assumptions: Published source summary, not a new mathematical assertion

entries.title: Biskup-Chayes mean-field free-energy excess bound
entries.statement: For d>=3, let spins S_x in a compact Omega subset of a finite-dimensional inner-product space E_Omega have an i.i.d. a priori law mu, with interaction -J/(2d) times the sum of nearest-neighbor inner products and field -sum_x(b,S_x), J>=0. Let S(m)=inf_h[log int_Omega exp((S,h)) mu(dS)-(m,h)] and Phi_{J,b}(m)=-J|m|^2/2-(m,b)-S(m). If F(J,b) is the thermodynamic free energy per site, let K*(J,b) be the supporting-hyperplane pairs (e,m) satisfying F(J+deltaJ,b+deltab)-F(J,b)<=e deltaJ+(m,deltab) for all increments; let M*(J,b) consist of magnetizations of extreme pairs of K*. For m* in M*(J,b), Phi_{J,b}(m*) <= inf_{m in Conv(Omega)} Phi_{J,b}(m) + J n kappa I_d/2. Here n=dim(E_Omega), kappa=max_{S in Omega}(S,S), D_d(k)=1-(1/d)sum_{j=1}^d cos(k_j), and I_d=int_{[-pi,pi]^d} (1-D_d(k))^2/D_d(k) dk/(2pi)^d. For the q-state Potts simplex representation this error is J(q-1)^2 I_d/(2q). This bound does not itself force a first-order transition at d=3,q=3.
entries.proof_text: The source proves its Main Theorem using reflection positivity and an infrared bound to control the difference between nearest-neighbor spin correlation and squared magnetization in extreme thermodynamic states; inserting that estimate into the general convexity bound (1.9) yields (1.12). The Potts coefficient follows by n=q-1 and kappa=(q-1)/q.
assumptions: compact Omega in a finite-dimensional inner-product space
i.i.d. Borel a priori spin law supported on Omega
m* belongs to M*(J,b) from extreme thermodynamic supporting-hyperplane points
reflection positivity and infrared bound for the source's interaction

entries.title: Biskup-Chayes Potts jump for fixed q and sufficiently large d
entries.statement: For each fixed integer q>=3, Biskup-Chayes Theorem 2.1 gives a coupling J_t(q,d) and errors epsilon_1(d,J), epsilon_2(d) tending to zero as d tends to infinity (epsilon_1 uniformly on bounded J intervals), such that m*(J)<=epsilon_1 for J<J_t, |m*(J)-m_MF(J)|<=epsilon_1 for J>J_t, and |J_t-J_MF|<=epsilon_2. For sufficiently large d, magnetization and energy density jump at J_t. Their theorem does not show m*(J)=0 throughout J<J_t and hence does not by itself identify J_t with the critical onset coupling required by C0048.
entries.proof_text: In the source's proof, the infrared error J(q-1)^2 I_d/(2q) tends to zero for fixed q as d grows. The mean-field Potts free energy has separated symmetric and asymmetric minima for q>=3. The small excess confines physical extreme magnetizations near these minima, and FK/FKG monotonicity yields a jump point J_t; free-energy comparison bounds its distance from J_MF. The paper explicitly leaves open whether small positive magnetization can occur before J_t.
assumptions: nearest-neighbor q-state ferromagnetic Potts model on Z^d
d sufficiently large depending on q for the jump conclusion
coupling J is normalized as J/(2d) per edge in Biskup-Chayes (2.1)
use of extreme-state mean-field bound and FK/FKG monotonicity

entries.title: C0048 draft gap: jump coupling versus critical onset
entries.statement: DRAFT GAP, not a theorem: C0048 asks for positive monochromatic-boundary magnetization at the true critical coupling J_c for every integer q>=3,d>=3. The Biskup-Chayes fixed-q/large-d jump theorem locates a jump J_t but explicitly does not exclude smaller positive magnetization for J<J_t. Its infrared error tends to zero with d and supplies no q=3,d=3 barrier. A valid bridge must identify or bypass the possible interval J_c<J_t and establish a bound effective at low d and small q; uniform pressure approximation alone cannot do this.
assumptions: Biskup-Chayes Theorem 2.1 and its explicit caveat
No claim that the full conjecture is proved

relations.rationale: The bound is the Main Theorem (1.12) in this paper.
The Potts jump proof uses the small infrared free-energy excess for extreme magnetizations.
The statement is Theorem 2.1 and the immediately following limitation in this paper.
The gap is the jump theorem's explicit inability to rule out ordered magnetization below J_t.
The published theorem concerns fixed-q, sufficiently-large-d Potts jumps; it does not alone establish C0048's critical-onset formulation.
This draft concept records the missing identification of J_t with critical onset and the q=3,d=3 quantitative barrier.
